newsitem.title: THAILAND: Banharn orders police to curb election violence.
newsitem.headline: Banharn orders police to curb election violence.

text.p: Thailand's caretaker prime minister, Banharn Silpa-archa, has ordered police to step up efforts to halt poll violence after a spate of shootings ahead of the November 17 election, police said on Sunday.
A politicial activist for the Democrat party was shot dead in Phichit province north of Bangkok on Saturday, while another party worker was injured in an attack in Samut Sakorn province.
Unidentified gunmen also fired on the house of the campaign manager for the Solidarity Party in Nakhon Phathom province on Saturday night, police said. No one was injured in the attack.
A total of six political workers, mostly from the opposition parties, have been shot dead since Wednesday, police said.
"I have ordered police to step up measures to prevent the violence despite the fact that some cases may not be related to the election," Banharn told reporters at a rally late on Saturday.
Seventeen people have been attacked by unidentified gunmen, seven of them killed, since campaigning began on September 27.
Campaigner workers are usually the prime targets for gunmen rather than candidates, police said. The workers are usually better known and more influential locally than the politicians.
Police have said they were monitoring some 750 known gumen to prevent them from harming the 2,310 politicians who are vying for the 393 seats up for grabs in the parliamentary poll.
The manager of a jungle trek shop told Reuters last week that he has sold out his stock of bullet-proof vests.
"I sold most of the body armour to the canvassers and now my store has already run out. A new shipment will arrive on Tuesday and it is all already pre-sold," he said, speaking anonymously.
